newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Q2 Special IPCA inflation index 1.74 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Q2 Special IPCA inflation index 1.74 pct.

text.p: Brazilian inflation as measured by the Special Wider National Consumer Price Index (IPCA-E) was 1.74 percent in the second quarter of 1997, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.

Inflation as measured by the index was 2.45 percent in the first quarter of this year. The second quarter result puts inflation since the start of the government's anti-inflationary real plan in July 1994 at 68.98 percent, the IBGE said.
The IPCA-E is a quarterly index based on the spending of families with an income of up to 40 minimum salaries. It is used to calculate the Ufir index which adjusts income tax.
So far this year, inflation stands at 4.23 percent as measured by the index, and 7.32 for the last twleve months.
In the three years of the Real Plan, the cost of housing has seen the greatest rise at 285.40 percent, followed by communications, up 244.92 percent, and personal services, which rose 134.54 percent.

Areas which saw an increase of less than 68.98 percent included TV and sound equipment which registered a rise of only 4.11 percent, sugar and derivatives, which advanced 11.56 percent, and jewelry and wrist watches, which rose 21.93 percent.

During the second quarter of this year, the rise in the cost of housing slowed down from 1.17 percent in April to 0.71 percent in May and 0.64 percent in June, with an accumulated total for the three-month period of 2.54 percent.

Communications however showed the highest increase, with a variation of 85.68 percent, followed by domestic combustibles, up 11.05 percent, and electric energy, which rose 8.86 percent. ((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
